rate-limiter.intro: A strong design makes the policy explicit, enforces it near the request path, and chooses a clear consistency tradeoff.

sections.title: Requirements and API
sections.body: Support per-API-key and per-endpoint limits, a configurable time window, and a clear 429 response with Retry-After. Clarify whether a short burst is allowed and whether limits are global or regional.

sections.title: Algorithm and storage
sections.body: Use a token bucket for a simple burst allowance and steady refill. Keep bucket state keyed by API key and policy. A fast in-memory or Redis-backed counter works at moderate scale; partition keys to spread hot traffic.

sections.title: Multi-region behavior
sections.body: For strict global quotas, route each key to a home region or use a coordinated shared store, accepting extra latency. If approximate limits are acceptable, allocate regional token budgets and reconcile asynchronously.

sections.title: Failure handling and operations
sections.body: Decide whether a limiter outage fails open or closed by endpoint risk. Protect the backing store with timeouts and local fallback limits. Track allowed and rejected requests, store latency, hot keys, and policy changes.

url-shortener.intro: Separate the write path that creates short codes from the latency-sensitive redirect path.

sections.title: API and data model
sections.body: POST /links creates a record containing code, destination, owner, and expiry. GET /{code} returns a redirect. Use a unique index on code and a collision-safe ID generator such as a sequence encoded in base62 or random codes with retry.

sections.title: Redirect path
sections.body: Check a CDN or regional cache first, then a replicated key-value store. Cache popular redirects with bounded TTL and invalidate on deletion or destination changes.

sections.title: Scale and correctness
sections.body: Estimate redirects far exceed writes. Partition by code hash, replicate for reads, and keep code generation independent from the redirect database where practical. Define behavior for expired, missing, and malicious links.

sections.title: Operations
sections.body: Add rate limits, phishing detection, abuse reporting, and click analytics through an asynchronous event stream so analytics do not slow redirects.

notification-service.intro: Model delivery as a durable workflow with per-channel queues, idempotency, and explicit provider feedback.

sections.title: Request and preferences
sections.body: Accept an idempotent notification request, resolve user preferences and consent, then create a durable notification record with channel, priority, and delivery state.

sections.title: Queues and workers
sections.body: Partition queues by recipient or tenant. Workers pull jobs and call email, push, or SMS providers with per-provider concurrency and rate limits. Retry transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter; dead-letter permanent failures.

sections.title: Delivery semantics
sections.body: Exactly-once delivery across external providers is generally unavailable. Use idempotency keys where supported, record attempts, and make duplicate delivery tolerable.

sections.title: Visibility and resilience
sections.body: Track queue age, provider success, retry counts, and end-to-end delivery time. Isolate provider outages and allow priority traffic to continue.

news-feed.intro: Choose a feed strategy based on the balance between write amplification and read latency, then make ranking and freshness explicit.

sections.title: Read and write paths
sections.body: For ordinary accounts, fan out new posts to follower inboxes on write for fast reads. For celebrity accounts, avoid massive write fan-out and merge their posts during reads.

sections.title: Feed storage
sections.body: Store ordered post IDs per user with timestamps and ranking metadata. Hydrate post details in batches from a cache and durable post store.

sections.title: Ranking and pagination
sections.body: Rank candidates using recency and product signals, and paginate with a stable cursor rather than offsets. Refresh asynchronously and provide a fallback when ranking is slow.

sections.title: Scale and quality
sections.body: Partition inboxes by user, cache the first page, and cap feed fan-out work. Monitor freshness, latency, duplicate rate, and engagement quality.

file-storage.intro: Keep file bytes in durable object storage and metadata in a transactional service, connected by a versioned sync protocol.

sections.title: Upload and storage
sections.body: Split large files into chunks, upload chunks with resumable IDs, then commit a manifest after integrity checks. Store immutable chunks in object storage and metadata separately.

sections.title: Sync and versioning
sections.body: Track a version vector or monotonically increasing revision per file. Devices request changes since their last revision; concurrent edits create explicit conflict copies or use a merge policy suited to file type.

sections.title: Sharing and security
sections.body: Represent access with ACLs or scoped share tokens. Check permissions on every metadata and download request, support revocation, and encrypt data in transit and at rest.

sections.title: Reliability
sections.body: Use checksums, replication, lifecycle policies, and restore tests. Monitor upload completion, sync lag, integrity errors, and storage costs.

metrics-platform.intro: Build a high-throughput ingestion path, control cardinality, and optimize storage for time-range queries and retention.

sections.title: Ingestion
sections.body: Agents batch and compress points, then publish to a partitioned stream. Validate schemas and apply backpressure or sampling when tenants exceed quotas.

sections.title: Storage and queries
sections.body: Partition by metric and time, organize data into time blocks, and use columnar compression. Keep recent data at high resolution and downsample older ranges.

sections.title: Cardinality and isolation
sections.body: Enforce label limits and identify expensive series before they overwhelm indexes. Separate tenant quotas and query budgets.

sections.title: Alerts and operations
sections.body: Evaluate alert rules close to the data, deduplicate notifications, and monitor ingestion lag, query latency, dropped points, and storage growth.

job-scheduler.intro: Separate durable schedule definitions from execution attempts, and make workers safe to retry after partial failure.

sections.title: Schedule storage
sections.body: Store each job’s next due time, recurrence rule, payload, and state. Partition due jobs by time bucket and shard so schedulers can scan bounded ranges.

sections.title: Claim and dispatch
sections.body: Schedulers atomically lease due jobs, enqueue execution records, and advance the next occurrence. Workers use lease expiry so abandoned jobs can be retried after crashes.

sections.title: Delivery guarantees
sections.body: At-least-once execution is practical; make handlers idempotent with job IDs. Retry transient errors with backoff and route exhausted jobs to a dead-letter state.

sections.title: Scale and correctness
sections.body: Use UTC timestamps, define recurrence and daylight-saving semantics, spread bursts with jitter, and track scheduling lag, retries, duplicate claims, and worker saturation.

systems.title: Design a rate limiter
systems.scenario: Design a rate limiter for a public API handling 1M requests per second across multiple regions.
guide: Clarify whether limits are per user, key, or endpoint and what consistency is required.
Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, and sliding window; explain the tradeoffs.
Choose an enforcement point and discuss distributed counters, hot keys, regional behavior, and cache.
Cover failure policy, abuse resistance, observability, and how you would test limits at scale.

systems.title: Design a URL shortener
systems.scenario: Design a URL shortener that supports 100M new links each month and fast global redirects.
guide: Estimate read/write volume and define expiry, custom aliases, and redirect requirements.
Choose an ID generation strategy and data model; discuss collision handling.
Cover cache, database partitioning, global reads, and consistency.
Add abuse controls, analytics, and operational metrics.

systems.title: Design a notification service
systems.scenario: Design a service that delivers email, push, and SMS notifications to 50M users.
guide: Clarify delivery guarantees, priority, preferences, and per-channel constraints.
Design queues and workers with deduplication, retries, and backoff.
Discuss provider failures, rate limits, ordering, and dead-letter handling.
Define delivery observability, privacy controls, and capacity planning.

systems.title: Design a news feed
systems.scenario: Design a personalized home feed for 100M users with low-latency reads.
guide: Compare fan-out on write and fan-out on read, including celebrity accounts.
Describe ranking inputs, pagination, and feed freshness.
Design cache keys and invalidation while managing hot users.
Discuss storage growth, backfills, and feed quality metrics.

systems.title: Design a file storage service
systems.scenario: Design a cloud file service that syncs large files across devices and supports sharing.
guide: Separate file metadata from blob storage and define chunking and resumable upload.
Cover sync protocol, versioning, and concurrent edit conflicts.
Discuss sharing permissions, encryption, and link revocation.
Address durability, replication, quotas, and recovery.

systems.title: Design a metrics platform
systems.scenario: Design an internal metrics platform ingesting millions of data points per second.
guide: Clarify query patterns, freshness, retention, and cardinality limits.
Design buffered ingestion and a time-series storage layout.
Cover downsampling, aggregation, alerting, and backpressure.
Define isolation, cost controls, and service-level objectives.

systems.title: Design a job scheduler
systems.scenario: Design a distributed scheduler that runs millions of delayed and recurring jobs.
guide: Define timing precision, recurring job semantics, and delivery guarantees.
Discuss sharding, safely claiming jobs, and worker coordination.
Cover retries, dead letters, fairness, and hot partitions.
Address clock issues, observability, and operational recovery.

trend.title: From copilots to agentic workflows
trend.intro: Production agent engineering centers on measuring outcomes, tracing the full run, and keeping permissions and escalation paths clear.

points.title: Measure outcomes
points.text: Build task-specific evaluations into the development loop.

points.title: Observe the whole run
points.text: Trace tool calls, latency, cost, and handoffs.

points.title: Keep control legible
points.text: Bound permissions and define human escalation paths.

trend.readingSummary: Agent reliability is becoming an engineering discipline: evaluation, observability, and deliberate context design show up alongside model choice.
